recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If the work group wants to further discourage iso21090-nullFlavor or prefer Data Absent Reason more strongly, open a new policy issue and coordinate it with the Extension Pack rather than treating it as an unapplied FHIR-2881 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-2881 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU1. It asked that v3-specific terminology such as nullFlavor not appear in the core specification except when discussing v3, CDA, RIM, or RMIM mappings, and requested searches for nullFlavor/null flavor to make resource wording non-v3-specific.
initial_application: Git-svn revision 3030, represented by commit ac1ed867441c5d426787214ad07a167716e3e61b, applied the issue with the subject 'task 2881: remove narrative references to nullFlavor'. It changed an Observation profile comment from 'data null flavor' to 'data absent reason' and removed 'nullflavor' from Person.deceased[x] rationale.
additional_context: Current source still has NullFlavor strings, but they are in allowed or later-approved contexts: RIM mappings in Observation, v3 comparison text, ISO 21090/nullFlavor extension guidance that now links to the Extension Pack, C-CDA/v3 example material, terminology value-set inclusions, and later decisions such as FHIR-31385 and FHIR-47558. The Extension Pack currently defines iso21090-nullFlavor as an active FHIR-I extension and warns that it is tied to v3.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. A targeted search of active XML short/definition/comment/requirements/description fields found no remaining resource-description prose using NullFlavor/null flavor, so no current core source edit is needed for FHIR-2881.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue added current primitive-extension guidance that names nullFlavor alongside DataAbsentReason when explaining required bindings. It was used only as context and was not decided here.

Later Applied issue explicitly added Quantity guidance allowing exceptional values to draw on Data Absent Reason or v3 NullFlavor code systems. It explains intentional current NullFlavor wording and was not decided here.
